post_text:
Stop trusting wall-clock timestamps for event ordering in distributed systems.

It is a race condition waiting to happen. 🕒

Network latency and clock skew turn "first" into "whenever" across a cluster.

If your logic depends on absolute time, you are building on sand.

- Use partition keys to force related events into a single consumer stream for guaranteed sequence.

- Implement idempotent handlers to safely ignore the inevitable duplicates and late arrivals.

- Attach monotonic version numbers to entities to detect and reject stale state transitions. 🛠️

A system that assumes order is a system that breaks under load.

We got lucky that time.
lesson_extracted: Distributed systems require logical sequence numbers and idempotency because physical timestamps are unreliable for ordering.
